report_name: QuickFox VPN Supply Chain Attack Delivers FDMTP Backdoor

threat_actors.name: Twill Typhoon
threat_actors.description: A Chinese state-sponsored APT group that conducted a long-running supply chain attack, active since at least August 2025, against the QuickFox VPN application to deliver the FDMTP backdoor to a targeted demographic of overseas Chinese users.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor Twill Typhoon compromised the software build or distribution process for the QuickFox VPN application, injecting malicious code into the installer to deliver the FDMTP backdoor.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: JavaScript
attack_patterns.description: Malicious JavaScript code was injected into an Electron renderer HTML file within the trojanized QuickFox installer, which then downloaded a second-stage JavaScript loader.

attack_patterns.name: Acquire Infrastructure: Domains
attack_patterns.description: The threat actor used the typosquatted domain 'cdns3.51quickfox.cn' to host and deliver the second-stage JavaScript loader.

attack_patterns.name: Software Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The second-stage loader profiled the victim's machine by checking for the presence of specific administrative tools, software development applications, translation software, or cryptocurrency-related applications to determine if the system was a target of interest.

attack_patterns.name: User Execution: Malicious File
attack_patterns.description: The attack chain is initiated when a user downloads and runs the trojanized QuickFox VPN installer for Windows.

malware.name: FDMTP
malware.description: A modular backdoor delivered as the final payload in the QuickFox supply chain attack. It is used for reconnaissance, data exfiltration, and downloading additional malicious modules.

tools.name: QuickFox
tools.description: A legitimate VPN and network acceleration tool for Windows, popular among overseas Chinese users, that was trojanized in a supply chain attack. The earliest known trojanized version was 3.0.51.0.

identities.name: QuickFox
identities.description: The software vendor whose VPN application was compromised in a supply chain attack by Twill Typhoon. The developers removed the malicious components in version 3.59.6 after a responsible disclosure.

infrastructure.name: FDMTP Loader C2 Domain
infrastructure.description: A typosquatted domain 'cdns3.51quickfox.cn' used to download the second-stage JavaScript loader for the FDMTP backdoor.
